content.title: About
content.content: Mahi Mahi (Coryphaena hippurus), also known as dolphin fish or goldfish, is a marine species found in warm oceanic waters. Wild‑caught specimens are flash‑frozen shortly after capture, preserving their natural flavor, texture, and nutrients. The fillet is light pink, tender, and mildly sweet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mahi Mahi can change its skin colour depending on mood and environment.
It can grow up to 1.5 m in length within a single year.
In the wild, Mahi Mahi migrates across open oceans, often following large plankton blooms.
Its meat is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids but contains less mercury than many larger predatory fish.
Culinary uses include grilling, baking, and serving with fresh salsas.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, reduce inflammation, and aid brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein essential for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Low mercury content
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, Mahi Mahi contains lower levels of mercury, making it a safer frequent choice.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, phosphorus and potassium, important for antioxidant protection, bone health and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may react to Mahi Mahi.

items.title: Sodium in frozen processing
items.content: Some frozen products are brined; check the label and rinse if you need to limit sodium.

items.title: Possible parasites
items.content: As with any wild fish, parasites can be present; proper cooking eliminates the risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mahi Mahi fillets can be grilled, baked, pan‑seared, or steamed. They pair well with citrus marinades, herbs, olive oil, and light sauces. Thaw in the refrigerator before cooking and pat dry with paper towels.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen Mahi Mahi at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Do not leave the fish at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
